# 1 Enoch Chapter 20 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 20 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 20:1 — "who watch" vs. "who keep watch" vs. "assigned to keep watch"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "holy-angels who watch" | Minimal, literal |
| LOGOS | "holy angels who keep watch" | Adds "keep" for idiomatic completeness |
| PNEUMA | "holy angels assigned to keep watch over creation" | Adds "assigned" and "over creation" for context |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "holy angels who keep watch." "Keep watch" is the natural English idiom for the angelic role (cf. the Hebrew Watchers). PNEUMA's addition of "over creation" is interpretive; "assigned" is implied but unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:2 — Tartarus

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "over Tartarus" | Retains the transliterated term |
| LOGOS | "over Tartarus" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "over Tartarus, the place of the damned" | Adds explanatory gloss |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "over Tartarus" without gloss. Tartarus is well enough known and the gloss is interpretive. A reader note could clarify.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---

## 20:4 — Raguel's domain: "world of the luminaries" vs. "world on behalf of the luminaries"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "takes-vengeance on the world of the luminaries" | Genitive: the luminaries' world |
| LOGOS | "takes vengeance on the world on behalf of the luminaries" | Ge'ez preposition read as agent |
| PNEUMA | "executes God's judgment against the world on behalf of the luminaries" | Clarifies agent as God |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "takes vengeance on the world on behalf of the luminaries." The Ge'ez preposition indicates Raguel acts for the luminaries. EMET's genitive "of the luminaries" creates an odd possessive. PNEUMA's "God's judgment" adds an unexpressed subject.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 20:8 — Remiel's domain: "those who rise" vs. "those who rise from the dead"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those who rise" | Minimal; Ge'ez 'ella yetnessa'u |
| LOGOS | "those who rise" | Same minimal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "those who will rise from the dead" | Adds "from the dead" for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS/EMET "those who rise." The eschatological sense of resurrection is clear from context; adding "from the dead" is explanatory but not strictly required. The terser rendering preserves the list's parallel structure.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/EMET.

---
